blocks.text: Yeh chapter 13 (Halogens) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har sawal 4 number ka hai (wazahat, equations, zaroorat ho to diagram), aur chapter ke numericals qadam ba qadam hal kiye gaye hain. Har sawal ka poora model jawab hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 Describe the atomic and physical properties of the common halogens (fluorine to iodine): electron structure, physical state, colour, and the trend in melting and boiling points. (4 marks)
(Aam halogens (fluorine se iodine) ki atomic aur physical properties bayan karein: electron structure, physical halat, rang, aur melting aur boiling points ka silsila.)
blocks.explanation:
Halogens Group 17 (VIIA) ke elements hain; yeh bohat reactive non-metals hain aur har halat mein diatomic molecules X₂ ki shakal mein hote hain.

Electron structure: har halogen ke outer shell mein saat electrons hain (ns²np⁵): F 2, 7 (2s²2p⁵); Cl 2, 8, 7 (3s²3p⁵); Br 2, 8, 18, 7 (4s²4p⁵); I 2, 8, 18, 18, 7 (5s²5p⁵).

Room temperature par halat aur rang: fluorine halki zard gas, chlorine sabz-zard gas, bromine surkhi-mayl bhoora volatile liquid jis ke fumes corrosive aur zehreele hain, aur iodine chamakdar greyish black solid jo sublime ho kar violet vapour banta hai. Chlorine se iodine tak rang gehre hote hain, molecules ke andar electron transitions se light ke absorption ki tabdeeli ki wajah se.

Melting aur boiling points group mein neeche barhte hain (Table 13.1), kyunke molecules bare aur London forces mazboot hoti hain:

book_ref.quote: Table 13.1 Atomic and Physical properties of the common halogens.

blocks.prompt:
2 What is volatility? Explain how London dispersion forces decide the volatility and the physical states of chlorine, bromine and iodine. Summarise the effect of molecular size in a table. (4 marks)
(Volatility kya hai? Wazahat karein ke London dispersion forces chlorine, bromine aur iodine ki volatility aur physical halat kaise tay karti hain. Molecular size ka asar table mein dein.)
blocks.explanation:
Volatility kisi substance ke aasani se bukharat (vapour) banne ko kehte hain; yeh boiling point ke ulat hai, yani zyada volatile substance ka boiling point kam hota hai.

Forces: halogen molecules non-polar hain, is liye in ke darmiyan instantaneous dipole-induced dipole (id-id, London dispersion) forces hoti hain. Yeh molecule ke size, shape aur polarizability par munhasar hain. Mazboot forces mein molecules ko liquid se gas phase mein alag karne ke liye zyada energy chahiye, is liye boiling point zyada aur volatility kam hoti hai.

Silsila: group mein neeche molecular mass aur outer shell ka size barhta hai aur London forces mazboot hoti hain, is liye chlorine se iodine tak volatility kam hoti hai.
• Chlorine: chhote molecules, kamzor id-id forces; room temperature par gas, sab se zyada volatile, hawa mein jaldi phailti hai.
• Bromine: bare molecules, mazboot forces; liquid, chlorine se kam lekin iodine se zyada volatile; aasani se urr kar zehreele fumes deta hai.
• Iodine: group mein sab se mazboot forces; solid, sab se kam volatile.

Size ka asar (Table 13.2):

book_ref.quote: Larger, more polarizable molecules with stronger London dispersion forces have higher boiling points and lower volatility.

blocks.prompt:
3 Discuss the bond strength of the halogen molecules with the help of Table 13.3. Why is fluorine an exception to the trend? (4 marks)
(Table 13.3 ki madad se halogen molecules ki bond strength par behes karein. Fluorine is silsile se mustasna (exception) kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Bond energies (Table 13.3): F₂ 156, Cl₂ 243, Br₂ 193, I₂ 151 kJ mol⁻¹.

Aam silsila: chlorine se iodine tak bond energy darja ba darja kam hoti hai. Group mein neeche atomic size barhta hai, is liye bond length lambi aur bond kamzor hota hai: Cl₂ (243) > Br₂ (193) > I₂ (151).

Fluorine exception: sirf size se F-F sab se mazboot hona chahiye, lekin yeh sirf 156 kJ mol⁻¹ hai, Cl-Cl aur Br-Br se kamzor. Fluorine atoms bohat chhote hain, is liye F₂ molecule mein dono atoms ke lone pairs (har atom par teen, Fig. 13.1) bohat qareeb hote hain. In lone pairs ka shadeed electron-electron repulsion (dhakelna) fluorine ki zyada electronegativity ke bawajood bond ko kamzor kar deta hai.

Majmooi tarteeb: Cl₂ > Br₂ > F₂ > I₂.

book_ref.quote: Due to the small size, there is significant electron–electron repulsion between the lone pairs on the fluorine atoms

blocks.prompt:
4 What happens when each halogen is added to aqueous solutions of the other halide ions? Write balanced ionic equations for the displacements that occur and explain the results using the E° values of Table 13.4. (4 marks)
(Jab har halogen ko doosre halide ions ke aqueous solutions mein dala jaye to kya hota hai? Hone wale displacements ki balanced ionic equations likhein aur Table 13.4 ki E° values se nataij samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Halogens oxidizing agents hain: yeh electrons le kar halide ions bante hain. Halogen apne neeche wale halogens ke halide ions ko oxidize karke displace karta hai.

Fluorine baqi tamam halide ions ko displace karta hai:
F₂(g) + 2Cl⁻(aq) → 2F⁻(aq) + Cl₂
F₂(g) + 2Br⁻(aq) → 2F⁻(aq) + Br₂
F₂(g) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2F⁻(aq) + I₂

Chlorine Br⁻ aur I⁻ ko displace karta hai:
Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂
Cl₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + I₂

Bromine sirf I⁻ ko displace karta hai: Br₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Br⁻ + I₂

Iodine kisi halide ion ko oxidize nahi kar sakta, is liye koi reaction nahi.

Wazahat: E° (X₂/X⁻) fluorine se iodine tak kam positive hoti hai, yani oxidizing power kam hoti hai. Zyada E° wala halogen kam E° wale halogen ke halide ion ko oxidize karta hai. Oxidizing power: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.

book_ref.quote: Fluorine molecule can oxidize and displace all the halide ions from their solutions

header: Jin halide ions ko displace karta hai

blocks.prompt:
5 Describe the reactions of fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine with hydrogen, giving the conditions and equations, and name the acid each hydrogen halide forms in water. (4 marks)
(Fluorine, chlorine, bromine aur iodine ke hydrogen se reactions shiraait aur equations ke saath bayan karein, aur har hydrogen halide ke paani mein banne wale acid ka naam likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Halogens hydrogen se react karke hydrogen halides banate hain: H₂ + X₂ → 2HX. Hydrogen halides be-rang gases hain jo paani mein hal ho kar hydrohalic acids banati hain. Hydrogen ke saath reactivity group mein neeche kam hoti hai: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.

Fluorine: kam temperature aur andhere mein bhi dhamake se react karta hai.
H₂(g) + F₂(g) → 2HF(g); paani mein HF hydrofluoric acid banati hai.

Chlorine: UV light ya spark ki mojoodgi mein aasani se react karke be-rang HCl gas banata hai.
H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g) (hν); paani mein hydrochloric acid banti hai.

Bromine: garam karne par hydrogen se react karta hai; reaction exothermic hai.
H₂(g) + Br₂(g) → 2HBr(g) (heat); HBr paani mein taqatwar hydrobromic acid banati hai.

Iodine: sirf zyada temperature par catalyst ki mojoodgi mein react karta hai; reaction reversible aur bohat aahista hai.
H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) (catalyst); HI paani mein hydroiodic acid banati hai.

book_ref.quote: When halogen elements react with hydrogen, they produce hydrogen halides.

blocks.prompt:
6 Compare the trend in the bond energies of the halogen molecules X₂ (Table 13.3) with that of the hydrogen halides H-X (Table 13.5). Explain why fluorine is out of order in X₂ but not in H-X, and state the order of thermal stability of HX. (4 marks)
(Halogen molecules X₂ (Table 13.3) aur hydrogen halides H-X (Table 13.5) ki bond energies ke silsile ka muqabla karein. Wazahat karein ke fluorine X₂ mein tarteeb se bahar kyun hai lekin H-X mein nahi, aur HX ki thermal stability ki tarteeb likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Qeematein: X₂: F₂ 156, Cl₂ 243, Br₂ 193, I₂ 151 kJ mol⁻¹. H-X: H-F 569, H-Cl 431, H-Br 366, H-I 299 kJ mol⁻¹.

X₂ ka silsila: Cl₂ se I₂ tak bond energy kam hoti hai kyunke bare atoms lambe aur kamzor bonds dete hain. F₂ exception hai: bohat chhote fluorine atoms ke lone pairs qareeb hote hain aur un ka shadeed repulsion F-F bond ko kamzor karta hai.

H-X ka silsila: bond dissociation energy H-F se H-I tak baqaida kam hoti hai, fluorine sab se upar. Fluorine ki zyada electronegativity aur chhota atomic radius hydrogen ke saath mazboot orbital overlap aur bohat mazboot H-F bond dete hain. Group mein neeche bara halogen atom kam overlap deta hai: H-Cl H-F se kamzor, H-Br aur kamzor, aur bohat bara iodine atom kamzor overlap aur sab se kamzor bond H-I deta hai.

Thermal stability H-X bond strength ke mutabiq hai: HF > HCl > HBr > HI. HF sab se zyada aur HI sab se kam thermally stable hai.

book_ref.quote: Bond strength between the hydrogen and the halogen atom in the H-X molecule explain this trend.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: X₂ mein dono atoms halogen hain, is liye do chhote F atoms ke lone pairs aik doosre ko dhakelte hain. H-F mein aik taraf hydrogen hai jis par koi lone pair nahi, is liye yeh repulsion nahi hota aur chhota F atom mazboot overlap deta hai. Isi liye F₂ kamzor lekin H-F sab se mazboot hai.

blocks.prompt:
7 Using Table 13.5, calculate the energy needed to break all the H-X bonds in 10.0 g of HF and in 10.0 g of HI (H = 1, F = 19; take I from Table 13.1). How many times greater is the first value, and what does this show about thermal stability? (4 marks)
(Table 13.5 se 10.0 g HF aur 10.0 g HI ke tamam H-X bonds todne ke liye energy nikalein (H = 1, F = 19; I Table 13.1 se lein). Pehli qeemat kitne guna zyada hai, aur is se thermal stability ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Mass aur molar mass se moles nikalein, phir fi mole bond dissociation energy se zarb dein.

book_ref.quote: The bond dissociation energy of H-F (569 kJ/mol) is the highest among the hydrogen halides.

steps: Molar masses: HF = 1 + 19 = 20 g mol⁻¹; HI = 1 + 126.9 = 127.9 g mol⁻¹.
HF ke liye energy = 0.500 × 569 = 284.5 kJ; HI ke liye energy = 0.0782 × 299 = 23.4 kJ.
Tanasub = 284.5/23.4 ≈ 12.2. HF ko kahin zyada energy chahiye (mazboot H-F bond, 569 kJ mol⁻¹), is liye HF sab se zyada aur HI (299 kJ mol⁻¹) sab se kam thermally stable hai.
blocks.final_answer: HF: 284.5 kJ; HI: 23.4 kJ; taqreeban 12 guna; HF HI se kahin zyada thermally stable hai.

blocks.prompt:
8 Explain, ion by ion, how electronegativity, ionic size and charge density decide the strength of fluoride, chloride, bromide and iodide ions as reducing agents. (4 marks)
(Ion ba ion wazahat karein ke electronegativity, ionic size aur charge density fluoride, chloride, bromide aur iodide ions ki reducing agent ke taur par taqat kaise tay karte hain.)
blocks.explanation:
Halide ion apna extra electron de kar reducing agent ka kaam karta hai. Group mein neeche electronegativity kam aur ionic radius zyada hota hai; is se charge density kam hoti hai aur electron dena aasan hota hai. Reducing power ki tarteeb: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻.

Fluoride (F⁻): fluorine bohat electronegative hai aur apne extra electron ko mazboot bond se pakarta hai. Chhote F⁻ ion ki charge density zyada hai jo use mustahkam rakhti hai, is liye woh electron mushkil se deta hai; F⁻ sab se kamzor reducing agent hai.

Chloride (Cl⁻): size bara aur chlorine fluorine se kam electronegative, is liye Cl⁻ F⁻ se taqatwar lekin Br⁻ aur I⁻ se kamzor reducing agent hai.

Bromide (Br⁻): bromine chlorine se kam electronegative hai; Br⁻ ka ionic radius bara aur charge density kam hai, is liye woh aasani se electron deta hai aur Cl⁻ se taqatwar hai.

Iodide (I⁻): iodine ki electronegativity bohat kam aur I⁻ bara hai, charge density kam, is liye woh sab se aasani se electron deta hai; I⁻ halides mein sab se taqatwar reducing agent hai.

book_ref.quote: This trend is mostly due to the decreasing electronegativity and increasing atomic radius down the group.

blocks.prompt:
9 Describe how aqueous silver nitrate followed by aqueous ammonia is used to identify fluoride, chloride, bromide and iodide ions. Give the equations and observations. (4 marks)
(Bayan karein ke aqueous silver nitrate aur us ke baad aqueous ammonia se fluoride, chloride, bromide aur iodide ions kaise pehchane jate hain. Equations aur mushahidat dein.)
blocks.explanation:
Qadam 1, aqueous AgNO₃: halide ions Ag⁺ se react karke insoluble silver halides banate hain: X⁻(aq) + Ag⁺(aq) → AgX(s). Yeh qualitative analysis mein silver nitrate test hai.
• F⁻: koi reaction nazar nahi aata, kyunke silver fluoride paani mein hal hai.
• Cl⁻: safed precipitate, Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s).
• Br⁻: cream rang ka precipitate, Ag⁺(aq) + Br⁻(aq) → AgBr(s).
• I⁻: zard precipitate, Ag⁺(aq) + I⁻(aq) → AgI(s).

Qadam 2, aqueous ammonia precipitates ki solubility check karta hai:
• AgCl dilute ammonia mein hal ho kar be-rang diamminesilver(I) complex banata hai: AgCl(s) + 2NH₃(aq) → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).
• AgBr sirf concentrated ammonia mein hal hota hai: AgBr(s) + 2NH₃(aq) → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺(aq) + Br⁻(aq).
• AgI na dilute na concentrated ammonia mein hal hota hai.
• F⁻ ka precipitate hi nahi, is liye ammonia ka koi asar nahi.

Khulasa (Table 13.6):

book_ref.quote: provides a systematic way to differentiate between halide ions

blocks.prompt:
10 A solution containing 1.17 g of sodium chloride is treated with excess aqueous silver nitrate. Calculate the mass of silver chloride precipitated, and the mass of ammonia needed to dissolve this precipitate completely in dilute aqueous ammonia (Na = 23, Ag = 108, N = 14, H = 1; Cl from Table 13.1). (4 marks)
(1.17 g sodium chloride wale solution mein zyada aqueous silver nitrate dala jata hai. Precipitate hone wale silver chloride ki mass, aur is precipitate ko dilute aqueous ammonia mein poori tarah hal karne ke liye ammonia ki mass nikalein (Na = 23, Ag = 108, N = 14, H = 1; Cl Table 13.1 se).)
blocks.explanation: Aik Cl⁻ se aik AgCl banta hai, aur har AgCl do NH₃ le kar [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ banata hai.

book_ref.quote: Silver chloride dissolves in dilute ammonia to form diamminesilver(1) complex.

steps: Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s); AgCl(s) + 2NH₃(aq) → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).
NaCl = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 g mol⁻¹; NaCl ke moles = 1.17/58.5 = 0.0200 mol = AgCl ke moles.
NH₃ ke moles = 2 × 0.0200 = 0.0400 mol; NH₃ = 14 + 3 = 17 g mol⁻¹; NH₃ ki mass = 0.0400 × 17 = 0.68 g.
blocks.final_answer: AgCl precipitate = 2.87 g; zaroori ammonia = 0.68 g.

blocks.prompt:
11 Describe the reactions of solid sodium fluoride, chloride, bromide and iodide with concentrated sulfuric acid. Give equations and observations and relate the differences to the reducing power of the halide ions. (4 marks)
(Solid sodium fluoride, chloride, bromide aur iodide ke concentrated sulfuric acid se reactions bayan karein. Equations aur mushahidat dein aur farq ko halide ions ki reducing power se jorein.)
blocks.explanation:
NaF: hydrogen fluoride ke fumes bante hain. NaF(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → NaHSO₄ + HF(g). HF kamzor reducing agent hai, is liye H₂SO₄ se aage react nahi karti.

NaCl: hydrogen chloride ke fumes bante hain. NaCl(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → NaHSO₄ + HCl(g). Aage reaction nahi.

NaBr: HBr ke bhaap-numa fumes, bromine ke bhoore fumes aur SO₂ ki boo. Yeh redox reaction hai:
NaBr + H₂SO₄(l) → NaHSO₄ + HBr(g)
2HBr(g) + H₂SO₄(l) → Br₂(g) + SO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)
HBr sulfuric acid ko SO₂ (S: +6 → +4) mein reduce karti hai aur khud bromine mein oxidize hoti hai.

NaI: HI ke fumes, iodine ke banafshi fumes aur H₂S ki boo:
NaI + H₂SO₄(l) → NaHSO₄ + HI(g)
8HI(g) + H₂SO₄(l) → 4I₂(s) + H₂S(g) + 4H₂O(l)
HI taqatwar reducing agent hai; yeh H₂SO₄ ko H₂S (S: +6 → -2) mein reduce karti hai aur khud I₂ mein oxidize hoti hai.

Taaluq: halide ions ki reducing power fluoride se iodide tak barhti hai, is liye reactions zyada pecheeda hote hain: F⁻ aur Cl⁻ sirf HX dete hain, Br⁻ acid ko SO₂ tak aur I⁻ H₂S tak reduce karta hai.

book_ref.quote: The nature of the product and nature of reaction changes down the group from fluoride to iodide.

blocks.prompt:
12 16.18 g of hydrogen bromide reacts completely with concentrated sulfuric acid according to the balanced equation 2HBr(g) + H₂SO₄(l) → Br₂(g) + SO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l). Calculate the masses of bromine and sulfur dioxide formed (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16; Br from Table 13.1), and show the change in oxidation state of sulfur. (4 marks)
(16.18 g hydrogen bromide concentrated sulfuric acid se balanced equation 2HBr(g) + H₂SO₄(l) → Br₂(g) + SO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l) ke mutabiq poori tarah react karti hai. Banne wale bromine aur sulfur dioxide ki masses nikalein (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16; Br Table 13.1 se), aur sulfur ki oxidation state ki tabdeeli dikhayein.)
blocks.explanation: Do moles HBr se aik mole Br₂ aur aik mole SO₂ banta hai.

book_ref.quote: Hydrogen bromide acts as a reducing agent by reducing sulfuric acid to sulfur dioxide and is self-oxidized to bromine.

steps: Br₂ ke moles = SO₂ ke moles = 0.200/2 = 0.100 mol.
Sulfur: H₂SO₄ mein +6 → SO₂ mein +4 (2 se reduce); bromine: HBr mein -1 → Br₂ mein 0 (do Br atoms aik aik electron dete hain).
blocks.final_answer: Br₂ = 15.98 g; SO₂ = 6.40 g; sulfur +6 se +4 tak reduce hota hai.

blocks.prompt:
13 Explain why the reaction of chlorine with hot aqueous sodium hydroxide is a disproportionation reaction, and balance its equation by matching the electrons lost and gained by chlorine. (4 marks)
(Wazahat karein ke chlorine ka garam aqueous sodium hydroxide se reaction disproportionation reaction kyun hai, aur chlorine ke diye aur liye gaye electrons barabar karke is ki equation balance karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Disproportionation: aisa reaction jis mein aik hi element aik saath oxidation aur reduction dono se guzre.

Garam NaOH ke products: sodium chloride (NaCl) aur sodium chlorate(V) (NaClO₃). Chlorine ki oxidation states: Cl₂ = 0, NaCl = -1, NaClO₃ = +5. Kuch chlorine reduce (0 → -1) aur kuch oxidize (0 → +5) aik hi reaction mein hoti hai, is liye yeh disproportionation hai.

Electrons se balance karna:
• Cl⁻ banne wala har Cl 1 electron leta hai.
• ClO₃⁻ banne wala har Cl 5 electrons deta hai.
• Electrons barabar karne ke liye har 1 oxidize hone wale Cl ke muqable mein 5 Cl reduce hone chahiyen: 6 Cl atoms = 3Cl₂.
• Is se 5NaCl aur 1NaClO₃ bante hain; sodium ke liye 6NaOH, aur hydrogen aur oxygen 3H₂O se barabar hote hain.

3Cl₂(g) + 6NaOH(aq) → 5NaCl(aq) + NaClO₃(aq) + 3H₂O(l)
Check: Cl 6 = 5 + 1; Na 6 = 5 + 1; O 6 = 3 + 3; H 6 = 6.

Thande NaOH mein oxidized product NaClO (chlorine +1) hota hai: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O. Yani temperature products tay karta hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Yaad rakhein: reduce hone wala chlorine sirf 1 electron leta hai, magar ClO₃⁻ banne wala chlorine 5 electrons deta hai. Isi liye 5 : 1 ka tanasub aata hai. Kitab ki chhapi equation mein NaCl ka coefficient 5 nahi tha; sahi equation upar di gayi hai.

blocks.prompt:
14 35.5 g of chlorine gas is passed into excess cold aqueous sodium hydroxide. Calculate the masses of NaOH used and of NaCl, NaClO and water formed, and show that mass is conserved (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1; Cl from Table 13.1). (4 marks)
(35.5 g chlorine gas zyada thande aqueous sodium hydroxide mein guzari jati hai. Istemal hone wale NaOH aur banne wale NaCl, NaClO aur paani ki masses nikalein, aur dikhayein ke mass mehfooz rehti hai (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1; Cl Table 13.1 se).)
blocks.explanation: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O istemal karein: aik mole Cl₂ ko do moles NaOH chahiye aur har product ka aik mole banta hai.

book_ref.quote: Chlorine undergoes disproportion when it reacts with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide

steps: Cl₂ = 71.0 g mol⁻¹; Cl₂ ke moles = 35.5/71.0 = 0.500 mol.
Istemal hone wala NaOH = 2 × 0.500 = 1.00 mol × 40 g mol⁻¹ = 40.0 g.
Reactants: 35.5 + 40.0 = 75.5 g; products: 29.25 + 37.25 + 9.0 = 75.5 g, is liye mass mehfooz hai.
blocks.final_answer: NaOH 40.0 g; NaCl 29.25 g; NaClO 37.25 g; H₂O 9.0 g (dono taraf kul 75.5 g).

blocks.prompt:
15 42.6 g of chlorine reacts completely with hot aqueous sodium hydroxide according to the balanced equation 3Cl₂ + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O. Calculate the masses of NaOH used and of NaCl and NaClO₃ formed (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1; Cl from Table 13.1). (4 marks)
(42.6 g chlorine garam aqueous sodium hydroxide se balanced equation 3Cl₂ + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O ke mutabiq poori tarah react karti hai. Istemal hone wale NaOH aur banne wale NaCl aur NaClO₃ ki masses nikalein (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1; Cl Table 13.1 se).)
blocks.explanation: Mole ratio Cl₂ : NaOH : NaCl : NaClO₃ = 3 : 6 : 5 : 1 istemal karein.

book_ref.quote: Chlorine is oxidized from 0 to +5 in NaClO₃.

steps: Cl₂ ke moles = 42.6/71.0 = 0.600 mol.
blocks.final_answer: Istemal hone wala NaOH 48.0 g; NaCl 58.5 g; NaClO₃ 21.3 g.

blocks.prompt:
16 How do the active species formed from chlorine in water destroy micro-organisms? Explain why HOCl is more effective than OCl⁻. (4 marks)
(Paani mein chlorine se banne wale active species micro-organisms ko kaise tabah karte hain? Wazahat karein ke HOCl OCl⁻ se zyada moassar kyun hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Active species ka banna: chlorine paani mein hydrolysis karti hai, Cl₂(g) + H₂O(l) → HCl(aq) + HClO(aq). Chloric(I) acid (hypochlorous acid, HOCl) kamzor acid hai aur jazwi tor par toot-ta hai: HOCl ⇌ H⁺ + OCl⁻ (chlorate(I) ya hypochlorite ion). HOCl aur OCl⁻ bunyadi active species hain.

Micro-organisms par asar (dono oxidizing agents hain):
• Yeh cell ke zaroori hisson jaise proteins aur lipids ko oxidize karte hain, jis se cell ka kaam bigar jata hai aur cell mar jata hai.
• Yeh bacteria ke zinda rehne aur replication ke liye zaroori enzymes ko oxidize karke na-kaara kar dete hain.
• Yeh nucleic acids (DNA aur RNA) ko oxidize karte hain, jis se bacteria replicate nahi kar sakte aur zaroori kaam ruk jate hain.

HOCl zyada moassar kyun: HOCl neutral (be-charge) hai, is liye micro-organisms ki cell walls mein aasani se dakhil hota hai; charged OCl⁻ ion kam moassar hai.

book_ref.quote: Essential cellular components such as proteins and lipids are oxidized by HOCl and OCl⁻

blocks.prompt:
17 Describe the factors that affect the disinfection of water by chlorine. Why is swimming-pool water given slightly more chlorine? (4 marks)
(Chlorine se paani ki disinfection par asar dalne wale factors bayan karein. Swimming pool ke paani mein thodi zyada chlorine kyun dali jati hai?)
blocks.explanation:
1. pH: pH taqreeban 6-7.5 par HOCl ghalib hota hai aur disinfection zyada moassar hoti hai. Zyada pH (7.5 se upar) par OCl⁻ ghalib hota hai; yeh kam moassar lekin phir bhi disinfection karta hai. (HOCl is liye behtar hai ke neutral hone ki wajah se cell walls mein dakhil ho jata hai.)

2. Chlorine dose (miqdaar): chlorine jitni zyada, disinfection utni moassar. Kaafi chlorine dalni chahiye taake bacteria marne ke liye kaafi HOCl aur OCl⁻ banein.

3. Contact time: paani aur chlorine ka raabta itna lamba ho ke disinfectants bacteria, viruses aur protozoa mein dakhil ho kar unhein maar sakein.

Swimming pools: paani mein bacteria zyada hone ka imkaan hai, is liye thodi zyada concentration mein chlorine dali jati hai. Thodi miqdaar mein chlorine insaanon ke liye be-zarar lekin beemari wale bacteria ke liye zehreeli hai, aur chlorination disinfection ka nisbatan sasta tareeqa hai.

book_ref.quote: At pH around 6-7.5, HOCl predominates and makes the disinfection process more effective.
